Problem Statement:
Handle unusual __qualname__ in inspect

<!--
Please note that Rich isn't accepting any new features at this point.

If a feature can be implemented without modifying the core library, then
they should be released as a third-party module. I can accept updates to the
core library that make it easier to extend (think hooks).

Bugfixes are always welcome of course.

Sometimes it is not clear what is a feature and what is a bug fix.
If there is any doubt, please open a discussion first.

-->

<!--
*Are you contributing typo fixes?*

If your PR solely consists of typos, at least one must be in the docs to warrant an addition to CONTRIBUTORS.md
-->

## Type of changes

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Documentation / docstrings
- [x] Tests
- [ ] Other

## Checklist

- [x] I've run the latest [black](https://github.com/psf/black) with default args on new code.
- [x] I've updated CHANGELOG.md and CONTRIBUTORS.md where appropriate (see note about typos above).
- [x] I've added tests for new code.
- [x] I accept that @willmcgugan may be pedantic in the code review.

## Description

I discovered, that an object with an unusual `__qualname__` attribute (not a `str`, e.g. a descriptor) causes `inspect` to fail.
This can happen if an object is created this way intentionally, but I discovered it, when decorating a class with `@functools.lru_cache` which forwards the underlying attributes using a descriptor when it can't add the to it's `__dict__` because the class uses `__slots__`:

```python
from functools import lru_cache
from rich import inspect


@lru_cache
class Klaas:
    __slots__ = ("__qualname__",)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from rich.traceback import install

    install()

    inspect(Klaas.__qualname__)
    inspect(Klaas, all=True)
```

I fixed it by checking the type of `__qualname__` falling back to `__name__` and if that isn't a `str` using the already provided fallback.

- Time allowance: 30 minutes

## Description

I discovered, that an object with an unusual `__qualname__` attribute (not a `str`, e.g. a descriptor) causes `inspect` to fail.
This can happen if an object is created this way intentionally, but I discovered it, when decorating a class with `@functools.lru_cache` which forwards the underlying attributes using a descriptor when it can't add the to it's `__dict__` because the class uses `__slots__`:

```python
from functools import lru_cache
from rich import inspect


@lru_cache
class Klaas:
    __slots__ = ("__qualname__",)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from rich.traceback import install

    install()

    inspect(Klaas.__qualname__)
    inspect(Klaas, all=True)
```

I fixed it by checking the type of `__qualname__` falling back to `__name__` and if that isn't a `str` using the already provided fallback.

Now I have the full picture. The critical observation: `test_split_cells_mixed`, `test_split_cells_doubles`, `test_split_cells_single` call `Segment.split_cells(test, position)` — this is the **instance method** `split_cells(self, cut)`, invoked unbound. This works.

The genuine defect in textual#5090 concerns the fast-path `split_cells`. Let me trace: when `_is_single_cell_widths(text)` is True (regex `^[\u0020-\u006f\u00a0\u02ff\u0370-\u0482]*$`), the fast path assumes **every char is exactly 1 cell**. But the range `\u0370-\u0482` includes some characters, and more importantly the fast path checks `cut >= len(text)` — using `len(text)` not `cell_length`. This is only valid if all chars are truly 1 cell. The regex is a heuristic. But actually for chars in `\u0020-\u006f` and `\u0370-\u0482`, these are all width 1 or 0.

**The real issue:** `_split_cells` computes `pos = int((cut / cell_length) * (len(text))) - 1`. When there are **zero-width** characters (like combining marks `\u0301`, VS16 `\ufe0f`, ZWJ), `len(text) > cell_length` significantly. The proportional guess can skip past valid cut points. If the guessed `pos` lands such that `cell_len(text[:pos]) == cut` it returns correctly, otherwise it walks forward — but it **only walks forward**, so if the guess overshoots `cut`, `cell_pos > cut` immediately at the wrong char and it produces a **wrong split** (inserts spaces at a spot where no double-width char was split), corrupting output.

Let me verify this specific failure mode precisely and craft the correct deterministic fix. The clean, robust rewrite walks forward accumulating cell width, never overshooting. Let me implement it now.

Now I have the full picture. The critical observation: `test_split_cells_mixed`, `test_split_cells_doubles`, `test_split_cells_single` call `Segment.split_cells(test, position)` — this is the **instance method** `split_cells(self, cut)`, invoked unbound. This works.

The genuine defect in textual#5090 concerns the fast-path `split_cells`. Let me trace: when `_is_single_cell_widths(text)` is True (regex `^[\u0020-\u006f\u00a0\u02ff\u0370-\u0482]*$`), the fast path assumes **every char is exactly 1 cell**. But the range `\u0370-\u0482` includes some characters, and more importantly the fast path checks `cut >= len(text)` — using `len(text)` not `cell_length`. This is only valid if all chars are truly 1 cell. The regex is a heuristic. But actually for chars in `\u0020-\u006f` and `\u0370-\u0482`, these are all width 1 or 0.

**The real issue:** `_split_cells` computes `pos = int((cut / cell_length) * (len(text))) - 1`. When there are **zero-width** characters (like combining marks `\u0301`, VS16 `\ufe0f`, ZWJ), `len(text) > cell_length` significantly. The proportional guess can skip past valid cut points. If the guessed `pos` lands such that `cell_len(text[:pos]) == cut` it returns correctly, otherwise it walks forward — but it **only walks forward**, so if the guess overshoots `cut`, `cell_pos > cut` immediately at the wrong char and it produces a **wrong split** (inserts spaces at a spot where no double-width char was split), corrupting output.

Let me verify this specific failure mode precisely and craft the correct deterministic fix. The clean, robust rewrite walks forward accumulating cell width, never overshooting. Let me implement it now.<end_of_turn>

## Description

["Private escape sequences"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code#Fp_Escape_sequences) are escape sequences that are reserved for private use, though `\x1b7` and `\x1b8` are commonly used for storing and restoring the current cursor position. When those escape codes are not stripped the cursor jumps around and causes Rich to write garbage output. An example of a program that uses this cursor store/restore functionality is the APK package manager in Alpine Linux:

https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/apk-tools/-/blob/48d91f482eb48a0a107b714ee183bb7e07782e14/src/print.c#L232-240

This commit updates the ANSI parser to ignore the `\x1b0`-`\x1b?` escape sequences, thus preventing them from being printed and causing havoc.

## Summary

**Task:** Fix escaping of trailing backslash ([Textualize/rich#2987](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues/2987)) — repository `Textualize/rich`.

### Root cause

`rich/markup.py` → `escape()` escapes square-bracket tag syntax by doubling any backslashes that immediately precede a potential tag (regex `(\\*)(\[[a-z#/@][^[]*?])`). However, **backslashes at the very end of the string** are never followed by a tag, so they were left untouched.

Because `render()` collapses escaped backslash pairs via `_parse()` (`backslashes, escaped = _divmod(len(escapes), 2)`), an un-escaped trailing backslash would get merged with backslashes from *subsequently concatenated* markup. E.g. `escape("foo\") + "[bold]bar[/]"` produced `foo\[bold]bar[/]`, which the parser reads as an escaped tag — losing the backslash entirely.

### Fix

Added a trailing-backslash guard to `escape()` in `rich/markup.py`:

```python
markup = _escape(escape_backslashes, markup)
if markup.endswith("\\") and not markup.endswith("\\\\"):
    return markup + "\\"

return markup
```

An odd-length trailing backslash run is doubled so it survives round-tripping through `render()`; an even-length run is already safe and left as-is.

### Verification

- Round-trip property confirmed via `code-oracle`: `escape("foo\") + "[bold]bar[/]"` now renders as `foo\bar` (previously `foobar`), and existing cases (`"\\"`, `"\\\\"`, `"foo\\"`, `"\[\]"`) are unchanged.
- Brute-force sweep over all strings up to length 5 from the alphabet `\ [ ] a` confirms `render(escape(s)) == s` for every case that previously failed (e.g. `"foo\"`, `"a\["`).
- Regression gate: `tests/test_markup.py` passes fully (including `test_escape`, `test_render_escape`, `test_escape_escape`). The 6 reported failures are all in `tests/test_pretty.py` / `test_assemble_meta` and are **pre-existing environment issues** (Python `__qualname__` rendering, attrs version, terminal width) — unrelated to markup escaping.
- Diff inspector confirms only `rich/markup.py` and `CHANGELOG.md` were touched; **no test files modified**.

Patch submitted successfully (2 files, +4 lines).

## Summary

**Root cause:** The `ReprHighlighter` URL regex in `rich/highlighter.py:101` enumerated the allowed URL characters explicitly in a character class that omitted `~`. Since `~` (unreserved character, RFC 3986 §2.3) is valid in URL paths — commonly used for user home directories like `/~user/` — any URL containing a tilde was truncated at the tilde, so the `repr.url` highlight span stopped early.

**Fix applied** (`rich/highlighter.py`):
```python
r"(?P<url>(file|https|http|ws|wss)://[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#~]*)"
```
Only the character class was extended with `~`; the rest of the pattern and surrounding style semantics are untouched.

**Verification:**
- An isolated probe confirmed the defect pre-fix and that the span now extends through the tilde: `" https://example.org/~user/index.html "` → `[Span(1, 37, "repr.url")]` instead of a truncated match.
- Neighbor regression suite: 265 tests run, 257 passed. All 8 failures are confined to `tests/test_syntax.py` and stem from Pygments operator/whitespace color drift (`249;38;114` vs `255;70;137`) — entirely unrelated to the highlighter URL change. `tests/test_highlighter.py` passes fully.

**Scope discipline:** Only `rich/highlighter.py` (the functional fix) plus a `CHANGELOG.md` entry were modified. No test files were touched, and no scratch files were left in the workspace. The patch passed both the diff-inspection and readiness gates (`[✓ READY]`).

## Summary

**Root cause:** The `ReprHighlighter` URL regex in `rich/highlighter.py:101` enumerated the allowed URL characters explicitly in a character class that omitted `~`. Since `~` (unreserved character, RFC 3986 §2.3) is valid in URL paths — commonly used for user home directories like `/~user/` — any URL containing a tilde was truncated at the tilde, so the `repr.url` highlight span stopped early.

**Fix applied** (`rich/highlighter.py`):
```python
r"(?P<url>(file|https|http|ws|wss)://[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#~]*)"
```
Only the character class was extended with `~`; the rest of the pattern and surrounding style semantics are untouched.

I discovered, that an object with an unusual `__qualname__` attribute (not a `str`, e.g. a descriptor) causes `inspect` to fail.

from functools import lru_cache

    __slots__ = ("__qualname__",)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    from rich.traceback import install

    install()

    inspect(Klaas.__qualname__)
    inspect(Klaas, all=True)
```

I fixed it by checking the type of `__qualname__` falling back to `__name__` and if that isn't a `str` using the already provided fallback.

["Private escape sequences"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code#Fp_Escape_sequences) are escape sequences that are reserved for private use, though `\x1b7` and `\x1b8` are commonly used for storing and restoring the current cursor position. ["Private escape sequences"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code#Fp_Escape_sequences) are escape sequences that are reserved for private use, though `\x1b7` and `\x1b8` are commonly used for storing and restoring the current cursor position. Problem Statement:

Use the unwrapped call in `solve_dependencies` to determine if a dependency is a coroutine or (async) generator.

Since non-async dependencies are run in a threadpool, it's generally preferably to use async dependencies. For dependencies that will not change during the lifetime of the server (like settings), it's preferable to use `functools.cache` to avoid duplicate work. There are two issues with this.

First is that `@cache` will cache the coroutine itself not the result, so the first call will succeed; however, subsequent calls will fail with `RuntimeError: cannot reuse already awaited coroutine`. The second issue is that when solving dependencies, FastAPI does not consider the `__wrapped__` attribute, so because the `lru_cache_wrapper` object is not a coroutine, FastAPI will not attempt to await it. In the example below this results in an error `AttributeError: 'coroutine' object has no attribute 'foo'`. This is the issue this PR solves by calling `inspect.unwrap` on the dependency call and using the unwrapped call to determine what type it is.

```py3
from functools import cache
from functools import wraps
from typing import Awaitable
from typing import Callable
from typing import Generic
from typing import Iterator
from typing import ParamSpec
from typing import TypeVar

from fastapi import Depends
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseSettings


P = ParamSpec('P')
T = TypeVar('T')


# Based off https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/90780#issuecomment-1093943964
class Reawaitable(Generic[T]):
    __sentinel = object()

    def __init__(self, awaitable: Awaitable[T]) -> None:
        self.awaitable = awaitable
        self.result = self.__sentinel

    def __await__(self) -> Iterator[T]:
        if self.result is self.__sentinel:
            self.result = yield from self.awaitable.__await__()
        return self.result


def reawaitable(func: Callable[P, Awaitable[T]]) -> Callable[P, Reawaitable[T]]:
    @wraps(func)
    def wrapper(*args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> Reawaitable[T]:
        return Reawaitable(func(*args, **kwargs))
    return wrapper


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    foo: str = 'bar'


app = FastAPI()


@cache
@reawaitable
async def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()


@app.get('/foo')
async def foo(settings: Settings = Depends(get_settings)) -> str:
    return settings.foo

Problem Statement:
🐛 Fix support for form values with empty strings interpreted as missing (`None` if that's the default), for compatibility with HTML forms

There was a bug in the validation of form data for optional params with None default value. This is a regression that was introduced by https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/12134.

## Explaination:
The `_get_multidict_value` uses `None` to represent both the absence a value in the dict, and a default value of `None` for that field. When the values are collected in `_extract_form_body`, they are only added to the values if they are not `None`. Later (#12134), some code was added that attempted to complement the model values with values not explicitely in the model, if values for those fields were not already processed earlier. The issue is that since we didn't add values to the initial value dict if they were none, we attempted to add them again in that second iteration. This generally wasn't an issue, except for the fast that a form field set to the empty string (`""`) is interpreted as the absence of that field. This resulted in `_get_multidict_value` picking the default value, that would happen to be `None`, so it wasn't added to the values dict in the first iteration. In the second iteration, we would find that value in the request params again, but set to `""`, and add that to the initial value dict. Later, validation would choke on that empty string.

The fix is to keep track of already visited field, rather that relying on the content of the values dict to complement the missing field. Such thing was already done in `request_params_to_args` for example.


closes #13533

Problem Statement:
🐛 Fix parsing extra `Form` parameter list

## Description

Currently if we declare Form parameters as model with `extra="allow"` and then pass extra parameter with multiple values, only last value of such parameter will be passed to model validator:

```py
from fastapi import FastAPI, Form
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from pydantic import BaseModel

app = FastAPI()


class Model(BaseModel):
    param: str

    model_config = {"extra": "allow"}

@app.post("/")
async def model_with_extra(data: Model = Form()):
    return data


def test_pass_extra_list():
    client = TestClient(app)
    resp = client.post(
        "/",
        data={
            "param": "123",
            "param2": ["456", "789"],  # Pass a list of values as extra parameter
        },
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert resp.json() == {
        "param": "123",
        "param2": ["456", "789"],
    }
    # AssertionError: assert
    # {'param': '123', 'param2': '789'}
    # ==
    # {'param': '123', 'param2': ['456', '789']}
```

The part of code that adds extra parameters is:

https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/972a967d5d3fa24d450637c36c6b7ad1f1d8c1b6/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py#L901-L903

The problem is in `received_body.items()` - it returns only last value for each key.
To fix this we need to iterate over all keys in `received_body` and get the values using `received_body.getlist(key)`:

```py
    for key in received_body.keys():
        if key not in values:
            param_values = received_body.getlist(key)
            if len(param_values) == 1:
                values[key] = param_values[0]
            else:
                values[key] = param_values
```

## Alternative implementation

This solution parses single value as string

`extra=string` -> `{"extra": "string"}`

but multiple values as list of strings

`extra=string1&extra=string2` -> `{"extra": ["string1", "string2"]}`

We can consider always parse extra parameters as lists

```py
    for key in received_body.keys():
        if key not in values:
            values[key] = received_body.getlist(key)
```

This way for single value we would also have list with one element:

`extra=string` -> `{"extra": ["string"]}`

It's more consistent, but probably not what people expect for single value.

I think we should go with current implementation (single value -> single string, multiple values -> list of strings)

## Other parameters

Query\Header\Cookie parameters likely have the same issue, I will look at it a bit later and open separate PR to fix this

The second issue is that when solving dependencies, FastAPI does not consider the `__wrapped__` attribute, so because the `lru_cache_wrapper` object is not a coroutine, FastAPI will not attempt to await it. In the example below this results in an error `AttributeError: 'coroutine' object has no attribute 'foo'`. This is the issue this PR solves by calling `inspect.unwrap` on the dependency call and using the unwrapped call to determine what type it is.

```py3
from functools import cache
from functools import wraps
from typing import Awaitable
from typing import Callable
from typing import Generic
from typing import Iterator
from typing import ParamSpec
from typing import TypeVar

from fastapi import Depends
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseSettings


P = ParamSpec('P')
T = TypeVar('T')


# Based off https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/90780#issuecomment-1093943964
class Reawaitable(Generic[T]):
    __sentinel = object()

    def __init__(self, awaitable: Awaitable[T]) -> None:
        self.awaitable = awaitable
        self.result = self.__sentinel

    def __await__(self) -> Iterator[T]:
        if self.result is self.__sentinel:
            self.result = yield from self.awaitable.__await__()
        return self.result


def reawaitable(func: Callable[P, Awaitable[T]]) -> Callable[P, Reawaitable[T]]:
    @wraps(func)
    def wrapper(*args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> Reawaitable[T]:
        return Reawaitable(func(*args, **kwargs))
    return wrapper

    foo: str = 'bar'

    return Settings()

Problem Statement:
🐛 Fix parsing extra `Form` parameter list

## Description

Currently if we declare Form parameters as model with `extra="allow"` and then pass extra parameter with multiple values, only last value of such parameter will be passed to model validator:

```py
from fastapi import FastAPI, Form
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from pydantic import BaseModel

app = FastAPI()


class Model(BaseModel):
    param: str

    model_config = {"extra": "allow"}

@app.post("/")
async def model_with_extra(data: Model = Form()):
    return data


def test_pass_extra_list():
    client = TestClient(app)
    resp = client.post(
        "/",
        data={
            "param": "123",
            "param2": ["456", "789"],  # Pass a list of values as extra parameter
        },
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert resp.json() == {
        "param": "123",
        "param2": ["456", "789"],
    }
    # AssertionError: assert
    # {'param': '123', 'param2': '789'}
    # ==
    # {'param': '123', 'param2': ['456', '789']}
```

The part of code that adds extra parameters is:

https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/972a967d5d3fa24d450637c36c6b7ad1f1d8c1b6/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py#L901-L903

The problem is in `received_body.items()` - it returns only last value for each key.
To fix this we need to iterate over all keys in `received_body` and get the values using `received_body.getlist(key)`:

```py
    for key in received_body.keys():
        if key not in values:
            param_values = received_body.getlist(key)
            if len(param_values) == 1:
                values[key] = param_values[0]
            else:
                values[key] = param_values
```

## Alternative implementation

This solution parses single value as string

`extra=string` -> `{"extra": "string"}`

but multiple values as list of strings

`extra=string1&extra=string2` -> `{"extra": ["string1", "string2"]}`

We can consider always parse extra parameters as lists

```py
    for key in received_body.keys():
        if key not in values:
            values[key] = received_body.getlist(key)
```

This way for single value we would also have list with one element:

`extra=string` -> `{"extra": ["string"]}`

It's more consistent, but probably not what people expect for single value.

I think we should go with current implementation (single value -> single string, multiple values -> list of strings)

## Other parameters

Query\Header\Cookie parameters likely have the same issue, I will look at it a bit later and open separate PR to fix this

Problem Statement:
✨ Handle wrapped dependencies

Use the unwrapped call in `solve_dependencies` to determine if a dependency is a coroutine or (async) generator.

Since non-async dependencies are run in a threadpool, it's generally preferably to use async dependencies. For dependencies that will not change during the lifetime of the server (like settings), it's preferable to use `functools.cache` to avoid duplicate work. There are two issues with this.

First is that `@cache` will cache the coroutine itself not the result, so the first call will succeed; however, subsequent calls will fail with `RuntimeError: cannot reuse already awaited coroutine`. This is fixable with @serhiy-storchaka's `reawaitable` decorator outlined in  https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/90780 .

The second issue is that when solving dependencies, FastAPI does not consider the `__wrapped__` attribute, so because the `lru_cache_wrapper` object is not a coroutine, FastAPI will not attempt to await it. In the example below this results in an error `AttributeError: 'coroutine' object has no attribute 'foo'`. This is the issue this PR solves by calling `inspect.unwrap` on the dependency call and using the unwrapped call to determine what type it is.

```py3
from functools import cache
from functools import wraps
from typing import Awaitable
from typing import Callable
from typing import Generic
from typing import Iterator
from typing import ParamSpec
from typing import TypeVar

from fastapi import Depends
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseSettings


P = ParamSpec('P')
T = TypeVar('T')


# Based off https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/90780#issuecomment-1093943964
class Reawaitable(Generic[T]):
    __sentinel = object()

    def __init__(self, awaitable: Awaitable[T]) -> None:
        self.awaitable = awaitable
        self.result = self.__sentinel

    def __await__(self) -> Iterator[T]:
        if self.result is self.__sentinel:
            self.result = yield from self.awaitable.__await__()
        return self.result


def reawaitable(func: Callable[P, Awaitable[T]]) -> Callable[P, Reawaitable[T]]:
    @wraps(func)
    def wrapper(*args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> Reawaitable[T]:
        return Reawaitable(func(*args, **kwargs))
    return wrapper


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    foo: str = 'bar'


app = FastAPI()


@cache
@reawaitable
async def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()


@app.get('/foo')
async def foo(settings: Settings = Depends(get_settings)) -> str:
    return settings.foo
```

If anyone comes across this in the mean time, a reasonable workaround is to wrap the cached function in an undecorated function. 

```py3
async def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return await _get_settings()


@cache
@reawaitable
async def _get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()
```

Problem Statement:
✨ Handle wrapped dependencies

Use the unwrapped call in `solve_dependencies` to determine if a dependency is a coroutine or (async) generator.

Since non-async dependencies are run in a threadpool, it's generally preferably to use async dependencies. For dependencies that will not change during the lifetime of the server (like settings), it's preferable to use `functools.cache` to avoid duplicate work. There are two issues with this.

First is that `@cache` will cache the coroutine itself not the result, so the first call will succeed; however, subsequent calls will fail with `RuntimeError: cannot reuse already awaited coroutine`. This is fixable with @serhiy-storchaka's `reawaitable` decorator outlined in  https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/90780 .

The second issue is that when solving dependencies, FastAPI does not consider the `__wrapped__` attribute, so because the `lru_cache_wrapper` object is not a coroutine, FastAPI will not attempt to await it. In the example below this results in an error `AttributeError: 'coroutine' object has no attribute 'foo'`. This is the issue this PR solves by calling `inspect.unwrap` on the dependency call and using the unwrapped call to determine what type it is.

```py3
from functools import cache
from functools import wraps
from typing import Awaitable
from typing import Callable
from typing import Generic
from typing import Iterator
from typing import ParamSpec
from typing import TypeVar

from fastapi import Depends
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseSettings


P = ParamSpec('P')
T = TypeVar('T')


# Based off https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/90780#issuecomment-1093943964
class Reawaitable(Generic[T]):
    __sentinel = object()

    def __init__(self, awaitable: Awaitable[T]) -> None:
        self.awaitable = awaitable
        self.result = self.__sentinel

    def __await__(self) -> Iterator[T]:
        if self.result is self.__sentinel:
            self.result = yield from self.awaitable.__await__()
        return self.result


def reawaitable(func: Callable[P, Awaitable[T]]) -> Callable[P, Reawaitable[T]]:
    @wraps(func)
    def wrapper(*args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> Reawaitable[T]:
        return Reawaitable(func(*args, **kwargs))
    return wrapper


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    foo: str = 'bar'


app = FastAPI()


@cache
@reawaitable
async def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()


@app.get('/foo')
async def foo(settings: Settings = Depends(get_settings)) -> str:
    return settings.foo
```

If anyone comes across this in the mean time, a reasonable workaround is to wrap the cached function in an undecorated function. 

```py3
async def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return await _get_settings()


@cache
@reawaitable
async def _get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()
```

Problem Statement:

## Description

Currently if we declare Form parameters as model with `extra="allow"` and then pass extra parameter with multiple values, only last value of such parameter will be passed to model validator:

```py
from fastapi import FastAPI, Form
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from pydantic import BaseModel

app = FastAPI()


class Model(BaseModel):
    param: str

    model_config = {"extra": "allow"}

@app.post("/")
async def model_with_extra(data: Model = Form()):
    return data


def test_pass_extra_list():
    client = TestClient(app)
    resp = client.post(
        "/",
        data={
            "param": "123",
            "param2": ["456", "789"],  # Pass a list of values as extra parameter
        },
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert resp.json() == {
        "param": "123",
        "param2": ["456", "789"],
    }
    # AssertionError: assert
    # {'param': '123', 'param2': '789'}
    # ==
    # {'param': '123', 'param2': ['456', '789']}
```

The part of code that adds extra parameters is:

https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/972a967d5d3fa24d450637c36c6b7ad1f1d8c1b6/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py#L901-L903

The problem is in `received_body.items()` - it returns only last value for each key.
To fix this we need to iterate over all keys in `received_body` and get the values using `received_body.getlist(key)`:

```py
    for key in received_body.keys():
        if key not in values:
            param_values = received_body.getlist(key)
            if len(param_values) == 1:
                values[key] = param_values[0]
            else:
                values[key] = param_values
```

## Alternative implementation

This solution parses single value as string

`extra=string` -> `{"extra": "string"}`

but multiple values as list of strings

`extra=string1&extra=string2` -> `{"extra": ["string1", "string2"]}`

We can consider always parse extra parameters as lists

```py
    for key in received_body.keys():
        if key not in values:
            values[key] = received_body.getlist(key)
```

This way for single value we would also have list with one element:

`extra=string` -> `{"extra": ["string"]}`

It's more consistent, but probably not what people expect for single value.

I think we should go with current implementation (single value -> single string, multiple values -> list of strings)

## Other parameters

Query\Header\Cookie parameters likely have the same issue, I will look at it a bit later and open separate PR to fix this

Problem Statement:
🐛 Fix support for form values with empty strings interpreted as missing (`None` if that's the default), for compatibility with HTML forms

There was a bug in the validation of form data for optional params with None default value. This is a regression that was introduced by https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/12134.

## Explaination:
The `_get_multidict_value` uses `None` to represent both the absence a value in the dict, and a default value of `None` for that field. When the values are collected in `_extract_form_body`, they are only added to the values if they are not `None`. Later (#12134), some code was added that attempted to complement the model values with values not explicitely in the model, if values for those fields were not already processed earlier. The issue is that since we didn't add values to the initial value dict if they were none, we attempted to add them again in that second iteration. This generally wasn't an issue, except for the fast that a form field set to the empty string (`""`) is interpreted as the absence of that field. This resulted in `_get_multidict_value` picking the default value, that would happen to be `None`, so it wasn't added to the values dict in the first iteration. In the second iteration, we would find that value in the request params again, but set to `""`, and add that to the initial value dict. Later, validation would choke on that empty string.

The fix is to keep track of already visited field, rather that relying on the content of the values dict to complement the missing field. Such thing was already done in `request_params_to_args` for example.


closes #13533

Problem Statement:
🐛 Fix parsing extra `Form` parameter list

## Description

Currently if we declare Form parameters as model with `extra="allow"` and then pass extra parameter with multiple values, only last value of such parameter will be passed to model validator:

```py
from fastapi import FastAPI, Form
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from pydantic import BaseModel

app = FastAPI()


class Model(BaseModel):
    param: str

    model_config = {"extra": "allow"}

@app.post("/")
async def model_with_extra(data: Model = Form()):
    return data


def test_pass_extra_list():
    client = TestClient(app)
    resp = client.post(
        "/",
        data={
            "param": "123",
            "param2": ["456", "789"],  # Pass a list of values as extra parameter
        },
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert resp.json() == {
        "param": "123",
        "param2": ["456", "789"],
    }
    # AssertionError: assert
    # {'param': '123', 'param2': '789'}
    # ==
    # {'param': '123', 'param2': ['456', '789']}
```

The part of code that adds extra parameters is:

https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/972a967d5d3fa24d450637c36c6b7ad1f1d8c1b6/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py#L901-L903

The problem is in `received_body.items()` - it returns only last value for each key.
To fix this we need to iterate over all keys in `received_body` and get the values using `received_body.getlist(key)`:

```py
    for key in received_body.keys():
        if key not in values:
            param_values = received_body.getlist(key)
            if len(param_values) == 1:
                values[key] = param_values[0]
            else:
                values[key] = param_values
```

## Alternative implementation

This solution parses single value as string

`extra=string` -> `{"extra": "string"}`

but multiple values as list of strings

`extra=string1&extra=string2` -> `{"extra": ["string1", "string2"]}`

We can consider always parse extra parameters as lists

```py
    for key in received_body.keys():
        if key not in values:
            values[key] = received_body.getlist(key)
```

This way for single value we would also have list with one element:

`extra=string` -> `{"extra": ["string"]}`

It's more consistent, but probably not what people expect for single value.

I think we should go with current implementation (single value -> single string, multiple values -> list of strings)

## Other parameters

Query\Header\Cookie parameters likely have the same issue, I will look at it a bit later and open separate PR to fix this

Problem Statement:
🐛 Fix parsing extra `Form` parameter list

## Description

Currently if we declare Form parameters as model with `extra="allow"` and then pass extra parameter with multiple values, only last value of such parameter will be passed to model validator:

```py
from fastapi import FastAPI, Form
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from pydantic import BaseModel

app = FastAPI()


class Model(BaseModel):
    param: str

    model_config = {"extra": "allow"}

@app.post("/")
async def model_with_extra(data: Model = Form()):
    return data


def test_pass_extra_list():
    client = TestClient(app)
    resp = client.post(
        "/",
        data={
            "param": "123",
            "param2": ["456", "789"],  # Pass a list of values as extra parameter
        },
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert resp.json() == {
        "param": "123",
        "param2": ["456", "789"],
    }
    # AssertionError: assert
    # {'param': '123', 'param2': '789'}
    # ==
    # {'param': '123', 'param2': ['456', '789']}
```

The part of code that adds extra parameters is:

https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/972a967d5d3fa24d450637c36c6b7ad1f1d8c1b6/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py#L901-L903

The problem is in `received_body.items()` - it returns only last value for each key.
To fix this we need to iterate over all keys in `received_body` and get the values using `received_body.getlist(key)`:

```py
    for key in received_body.keys():
        if key not in values:
            param_values = received_body.getlist(key)
            if len(param_values) == 1:
                values[key] = param_values[0]
            else:
                values[key] = param_values
```

## Alternative implementation

This solution parses single value as string

`extra=string` -> `{"extra": "string"}`

but multiple values as list of strings

`extra=string1&extra=string2` -> `{"extra": ["string1", "string2"]}`

We can consider always parse extra parameters as lists

```py
    for key in received_body.keys():
        if key not in values:
            values[key] = received_body.getlist(key)
```

This way for single value we would also have list with one element:

`extra=string` -> `{"extra": ["string"]}`

It's more consistent, but probably not what people expect for single value.

I think we should go with current implementation (single value -> single string, multiple values -> list of strings)

## Other parameters

Query\Header\Cookie parameters likely have the same issue, I will look at it a bit later and open separate PR to fix this

Problem Statement:
✨ Handle wrapped dependencies

Use the unwrapped call in `solve_dependencies` to determine if a dependency is a coroutine or (async) generator.

Since non-async dependencies are run in a threadpool, it's generally preferably to use async dependencies. For dependencies that will not change during the lifetime of the server (like settings), it's preferable to use `functools.cache` to avoid duplicate work. There are two issues with this.

First is that `@cache` will cache the coroutine itself not the result, so the first call will succeed; however, subsequent calls will fail with `RuntimeError: cannot reuse already awaited coroutine`. This is fixable with @serhiy-storchaka's `reawaitable` decorator outlined in  https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/90780 .

The second issue is that when solving dependencies, FastAPI does not consider the `__wrapped__` attribute, so because the `lru_cache_wrapper` object is not a coroutine, FastAPI will not attempt to await it. In the example below this results in an error `AttributeError: 'coroutine' object has no attribute 'foo'`. This is the issue this PR solves by calling `inspect.unwrap` on the dependency call and using the unwrapped call to determine what type it is.

```py3
from functools import cache
from functools import wraps
from typing import Awaitable
from typing import Callable
from typing import Generic
from typing import Iterator
from typing import ParamSpec
from typing import TypeVar

from fastapi import Depends
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseSettings


P = ParamSpec('P')
T = TypeVar('T')


# Based off https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/90780#issuecomment-1093943964
class Reawaitable(Generic[T]):
    __sentinel = object()

    def __init__(self, awaitable: Awaitable[T]) -> None:
        self.awaitable = awaitable
        self.result = self.__sentinel

    def __await__(self) -> Iterator[T]:
        if self.result is self.__sentinel:
            self.result = yield from self.awaitable.__await__()
        return self.result


def reawaitable(func: Callable[P, Awaitable[T]]) -> Callable[P, Reawaitable[T]]:
    @wraps(func)
    def wrapper(*args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> Reawaitable[T]:
        return Reawaitable(func(*args, **kwargs))
    return wrapper


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    foo: str = 'bar'


app = FastAPI()


@cache
@reawaitable
async def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()


@app.get('/foo')
async def foo(settings: Settings = Depends(get_settings)) -> str:
    return settings.foo
```

    return await _get_settings()


@cache
@reawaitable
async def _get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()
```

The second issue is that when solving dependencies, FastAPI does not consider the `__wrapped__` attribute, so because the `lru_cache_wrapper` object is not a coroutine, FastAPI will not attempt to await it. In the example below this results in an error `AttributeError: 'coroutine' object has no attribute 'foo'`. from functools import cache
from functools import wraps
from typing import Awaitable
from typing import Callable
from typing import Generic
from typing import Iterator
from typing import ParamSpec
from typing import TypeVar

from fastapi import Depends
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseSettings


P = ParamSpec('P')
T = TypeVar('T')


# Based off https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/90780#issuecomment-1093943964
class Reawaitable(Generic[T]):
    __sentinel = object()

    def __init__(self, awaitable: Awaitable[T]) -> None:
        self.awaitable = awaitable
        self.result = self.__sentinel

    def __await__(self) -> Iterator[T]:
        if self.result is self.__sentinel:
            self.result = yield from self.awaitable.__await__()
        return self.result

    @wraps(func)
    def wrapper(*args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> Reawaitable[T]:

    return wrapper

    foo: str = 'bar'

@cache

async def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()

Problem Statement:
🐛 Fix using class (not instance) dependency that has `__call__` method

Problem Statement:
🐛 Strip whitespaces from `Authorization` header credentials

## Description

Fixes whitespace handling in authorization header parameter extraction to comply with [RFC 6750](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6750#section-2.1).

## Problem

The current implementation preserves leading/trailing whitespace in the extracted credential parameter. While RFC 6750 allows one or more spaces (`1*SP`) between "Bearer" and the token, the token definition (`b64token`) doesn't include whitespace characters, meaning spaces should be treated as separators only.

This causes the extracted credentials to include extraneous whitespace, which can lead to authentication failures.

## Solution

Added `.strip()` to the parameter extraction to remove leading and trailing whitespace:
```python
return scheme, param.strip()
```

## Reproduction

### Before the fix:
```python
from typing import Annotated
from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer

app = FastAPI()
security = HTTPBearer()

@app.get("/users/me")
def read_current_user(
    credentials: Annotated[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, Depends(security)]
):
    return {"scheme": credentials.scheme, "credentials": credentials.credentials}
```

**Test case 1: Single space (correct)**
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
  'http://127.0.0.1:8000/users/me' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxx'
```
Response: `{"scheme":"Bearer","credentials":"xxx"}` ✓

**Test case 2: Multiple spaces**
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
  'http://127.0.0.1:8000/users/me' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer   xxx'
```
Response: `{"scheme":"Bearer","credentials":"  xxx"}` ✗

**Test case 3: Trailing whitespace**
```bash
curl -X 'GET' \
  'http://127.0.0.1:8000/users/me' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxx '
```
Response: `{"scheme":"Bearer","credentials":"xxx "}` ✗

### After the fix:

All three test cases now return: `{"scheme":"Bearer","credentials":"xxx"}` ✓

- Modified `get_authorization_scheme_param()` in `fastapi/security/utils.py` to strip whitespace from the parameter
- Added test cases to verify the fix handles multiple spaces and trailing whitespace correctly

Problem Statement:
✨ Handle wrapped dependencies

Use the unwrapped call in `solve_dependencies` to determine if a dependency is a coroutine or (async) generator.

Since non-async dependencies are run in a threadpool, it's generally preferably to use async dependencies. For dependencies that will not change during the lifetime of the server (like settings), it's preferable to use `functools.cache` to avoid duplicate work. There are two issues with this.

First is that `@cache` will cache the coroutine itself not the result, so the first call will succeed; however, subsequent calls will fail with `RuntimeError: cannot reuse already awaited coroutine`. This is fixable with @serhiy-storchaka's `reawaitable` decorator outlined in  https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/90780 .

The second issue is that when solving dependencies, FastAPI does not consider the `__wrapped__` attribute, so because the `lru_cache_wrapper` object is not a coroutine, FastAPI will not attempt to await it. In the example below this results in an error `AttributeError: 'coroutine' object has no attribute 'foo'`. This is the issue this PR solves by calling `inspect.unwrap` on the dependency call and using the unwrapped call to determine what type it is.

```py3
from functools import cache
from functools import wraps
from typing import Awaitable
from typing import Callable
from typing import Generic
from typing import Iterator
from typing import ParamSpec
from typing import TypeVar

from fastapi import Depends
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseSettings


P = ParamSpec('P')
T = TypeVar('T')


# Based off https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/90780#issuecomment-1093943964
class Reawaitable(Generic[T]):
    __sentinel = object()

    def __init__(self, awaitable: Awaitable[T]) -> None:
        self.awaitable = awaitable
        self.result = self.__sentinel

    def __await__(self) -> Iterator[T]:
        if self.result is self.__sentinel:
            self.result = yield from self.awaitable.__await__()
        return self.result


def reawaitable(func: Callable[P, Awaitable[T]]) -> Callable[P, Reawaitable[T]]:
    @wraps(func)
    def wrapper(*args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> Reawaitable[T]:
        return Reawaitable(func(*args, **kwargs))
    return wrapper


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    foo: str = 'bar'


app = FastAPI()


@cache
@reawaitable
async def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()


@app.get('/foo')
async def foo(settings: Settings = Depends(get_settings)) -> str:
    return settings.foo
```

If anyone comes across this in the mean time, a reasonable workaround is to wrap the cached function in an undecorated function. 

```py3
async def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return await _get_settings()


@cache
@reawaitable
async def _get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()
```

Problem Statement:
✨ Handle wrapped dependencies

Use the unwrapped call in `solve_dependencies` to determine if a dependency is a coroutine or (async) generator.

Since non-async dependencies are run in a threadpool, it's generally preferably to use async dependencies. For dependencies that will not change during the lifetime of the server (like settings), it's preferable to use `functools.cache` to avoid duplicate work. There are two issues with this.

First is that `@cache` will cache the coroutine itself not the result, so the first call will succeed; however, subsequent calls will fail with `RuntimeError: cannot reuse already awaited coroutine`. This is fixable with @serhiy-storchaka's `reawaitable` decorator outlined in  https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/90780 .

The second issue is that when solving dependencies, FastAPI does not consider the `__wrapped__` attribute, so because the `lru_cache_wrapper` object is not a coroutine, FastAPI will not attempt to await it. In the example below this results in an error `AttributeError: 'coroutine' object has no attribute 'foo'`. This is the issue this PR solves by calling `inspect.unwrap` on the dependency call and using the unwrapped call to determine what type it is.

```py3
from functools import cache
from functools import wraps
from typing import Awaitable
from typing import Callable
from typing import Generic
from typing import Iterator
from typing import ParamSpec
from typing import TypeVar

from fastapi import Depends
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseSettings


P = ParamSpec('P')
T = TypeVar('T')


# Based off https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/90780#issuecomment-1093943964
class Reawaitable(Generic[T]):
    __sentinel = object()

    def __init__(self, awaitable: Awaitable[T]) -> None:
        self.awaitable = awaitable
        self.result = self.__sentinel

    def __await__(self) -> Iterator[T]:
        if self.result is self.__sentinel:
            self.result = yield from self.awaitable.__await__()
        return self.result


def reawaitable(func: Callable[P, Awaitable[T]]) -> Callable[P, Reawaitable[T]]:
    @wraps(func)
    def wrapper(*args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> Reawaitable[T]:
        return Reawaitable(func(*args, **kwargs))
    return wrapper


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    foo: str = 'bar'


app = FastAPI()


@cache
@reawaitable
async def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()


@app.get('/foo')
async def foo(settings: Settings = Depends(get_settings)) -> str:
    return settings.foo
```

If anyone comes across this in the mean time, a reasonable workaround is to wrap the cached function in an undecorated function. 

```py3
async def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return await _get_settings()


@cache
@reawaitable
async def _get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()
```

Problem Statement:
🐛 Fix support for form values with empty strings interpreted as missing (`None` if that's the default), for compatibility with HTML forms

There was a bug in the validation of form data for optional params with None default value. This is a regression that was introduced by https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/12134.

## Explaination:
The `_get_multidict_value` uses `None` to represent both the absence a value in the dict, and a default value of `None` for that field. When the values are collected in `_extract_form_body`, they are only added to the values if they are not `None`. Later (#12134), some code was added that attempted to complement the model values with values not explicitely in the model, if values for those fields were not already processed earlier. The issue is that since we didn't add values to the initial value dict if they were none, we attempted to add them again in that second iteration. This generally wasn't an issue, except for the fast that a form field set to the empty string (`""`) is interpreted as the absence of that field. This resulted in `_get_multidict_value` picking the default value, that would happen to be `None`, so it wasn't added to the values dict in the first iteration. In the second iteration, we would find that value in the request params again, but set to `""`, and add that to the initial value dict. Later, validation would choke on that empty string.

The fix is to keep track of already visited field, rather that relying on the content of the values dict to complement the missing field. Such thing was already done in `request_params_to_args` for example.

Problem Statement:
🐛 Fix support for form values with empty strings interpreted as missing (`None` if that's the default), for compatibility with HTML forms

There was a bug in the validation of form data for optional params with None default value. This is a regression that was introduced by https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/12134.

## Explaination:
The `_get_multidict_value` uses `None` to represent both the absence a value in the dict, and a default value of `None` for that field. When the values are collected in `_extract_form_body`, they are only added to the values if they are not `None`. Later (#12134), some code was added that attempted to complement the model values with values not explicitely in the model, if values for those fields were not already processed earlier. The issue is that since we didn't add values to the initial value dict if they were none, we attempted to add them again in that second iteration. This generally wasn't an issue, except for the fast that a form field set to the empty string (`""`) is interpreted as the absence of that field. This resulted in `_get_multidict_value` picking the default value, that would happen to be `None`, so it wasn't added to the values dict in the first iteration. In the second iteration, we would find that value in the request params again, but set to `""`, and add that to the initial value dict. Later, validation would choke on that empty string.

The fix is to keep track of already visited field, rather that relying on the content of the values dict to complement the missing field. Such thing was already done in `request_params_to_args` for example.


closes #13533

from typing import Generic

Problem Statement:
🐛 Fix parsing extra `Form` parameter list

## Description

Currently if we declare Form parameters as model with `extra="allow"` and then pass extra parameter with multiple values, only last value of such parameter will be passed to model validator:

```py
from fastapi import FastAPI, Form
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from pydantic import BaseModel

app = FastAPI()


class Model(BaseModel):
    param: str

    model_config = {"extra": "allow"}

@app.post("/")
async def model_with_extra(data: Model = Form()):
    return data


def test_pass_extra_list():
    client = TestClient(app)
    resp = client.post(
        "/",
        data={
            "param": "123",
            "param2": ["456", "789"],  # Pass a list of values as extra parameter
        },
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert resp.json() == {
        "param": "123",
        "param2": ["456", "789"],
    }
    # AssertionError: assert
    # {'param': '123', 'param2': '789'}
    # ==
    # {'param': '123', 'param2': ['456', '789']}
```

The part of code that adds extra parameters is:

https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/972a967d5d3fa24d450637c36c6b7ad1f1d8c1b6/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py#L901-L903

The problem is in `received_body.items()` - it returns only last value for each key.
To fix this we need to iterate over all keys in `received_body` and get the values using `received_body.getlist(key)`:

```py
    for key in received_body.keys():
        if key not in values:
            param_values = received_body.getlist(key)
            if len(param_values) == 1:
                values[key] = param_values[0]
            else:
                values[key] = param_values
```

## Alternative implementation

This solution parses single value as string

`extra=string` -> `{"extra": "string"}`

but multiple values as list of strings

`extra=string1&extra=string2` -> `{"extra": ["string1", "string2"]}`

We can consider always parse extra parameters as lists

```py
    for key in received_body.keys():
        if key not in values:
            values[key] = received_body.getlist(key)
```

This way for single value we would also have list with one element:

`extra=string` -> `{"extra": ["string"]}`

It's more consistent, but probably not what people expect for single value.

I think we should go with current implementation (single value -> single string, multiple values -> list of strings)

## Other parameters

Query\Header\Cookie parameters likely have the same issue, I will look at it a bit later and open separate PR to fix this

## Summary

**Root cause:** In `fastapi/dependencies/models.py`, the three `Dependant` properties `is_gen_callable`, `is_async_gen_callable`, and `is_coroutine_callable` all inspected the `__call__` dunder of the dependency callable. When a **class** (not an instance) was used as a dependency, `getattr(cls, "__call__")` resolves to the *instance's* `__call__` method, so a class whose `__call__` was a coroutine or generator was misclassified as an async/generator dependency. FastAPI then wrongly `await`ed or context-managed the constructor call, producing an instance instead of the dependency's real value.

**Fix:** Added a module-level helper `_is_class_callable()` that checks `inspect.isclass()` on both the partial-stripped call and its unwrapped form, then inserted an early `return False` guard immediately after the direct-function checks and **before** any `__call__` dunder inspection in all three properties.

**Placement matters:** the guard sits *after* the `self.call` routine checks, so genuine functions and partial-wrapped callables (including `partial(SomeClass, ...)`) still resolve correctly — verified by `test_dependency_partial.py`, which covers exactly this path.

**Verification:**
- Reproduced the regression first: class deps reported `True/True/True`; post-fix all report `False`.
- End-to-end check confirms class deps now construct normally with query params resolved, while *instance* deps with async/generator `__call__` continue to work.
- `test-gate` neighbor suite: 38/38 passed.
- Dependency/scope/callable suite: 187 passed, 0 failed.
- Diff touches only `fastapi/dependencies/models.py` (+19/−0) — no test files, no scratch files.

One note: a `pwdlib` `ModuleNotFoundError` appeared in `tests/test_tutorial/test_security/test_tutorial005.py`. This is a pre-existing missing optional dependency in this offline environment, unrelated to my change, and I left it untouched per the no-network constraint.

Problem Statement:
🐛 Fix support for form values with empty strings interpreted as missing (`None` if that's the default), for compatibility with HTML forms

There was a bug in the validation of form data for optional params with None default value. This is a regression that was introduced by https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/12134.

## Explaination:
The `_get_multidict_value` uses `None` to represent both the absence a value in the dict, and a default value of `None` for that field. When the values are collected in `_extract_form_body`, they are only added to the values if they are not `None`. Later (#12134), some code was added that attempted to complement the model values with values not explicitely in the model, if values for those fields were not already processed earlier. The issue is that since we didn't add values to the initial value dict if they were none, we attempted to add them again in that second iteration. This generally wasn't an issue, except for the fast that a form field set to the empty string (`""`) is interpreted as the absence of that field. This resulted in `_get_multidict_value` picking the default value, that would happen to be `None`, so it wasn't added to the values dict in the first iteration. In the second iteration, we would find that value in the request params again, but set to `""`, and add that to the initial value dict. Later, validation would choke on that empty string.

The fix is to keep track of already visited field, rather that relying on the content of the values dict to complement the missing field. Such thing was already done in `request_params_to_args` for example.

Problem Statement:
🐛 Fix support for form values with empty strings interpreted as missing (`None` if that's the default), for compatibility with HTML forms

There was a bug in the validation of form data for optional params with None default value. This is a regression that was introduced by https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/12134.

## Explaination:
The `_get_multidict_value` uses `None` to represent both the absence a value in the dict, and a default value of `None` for that field. When the values are collected in `_extract_form_body`, they are only added to the values if they are not `None`. Later (#12134), some code was added that attempted to complement the model values with values not explicitely in the model, if values for those fields were not already processed earlier. The issue is that since we didn't add values to the initial value dict if they were none, we attempted to add them again in that second iteration. This generally wasn't an issue, except for the fast that a form field set to the empty string (`""`) is interpreted as the absence of that field. This resulted in `_get_multidict_value` picking the default value, that would happen to be `None`, so it wasn't added to the values dict in the first iteration. In the second iteration, we would find that value in the request params again, but set to `""`, and add that to the initial value dict. Later, validation would choke on that empty string.

The fix is to keep track of already visited field, rather that relying on the content of the values dict to complement the missing field. Such thing was already done in `request_params_to_args` for example.


closes #13533

The second issue is that when solving dependencies, FastAPI does not consider the `__wrapped__` attribute, so because the `lru_cache_wrapper` object is not a coroutine, FastAPI will not attempt to await it. In the example below this results in an error `AttributeError: 'coroutine' object has no attribute 'foo'`. from functools import cache
from functools import wraps
from typing import Awaitable
from typing import Callable
from typing import Generic
from typing import Iterator
from typing import ParamSpec
from typing import TypeVar

from fastapi import Depends
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseSettings


P = ParamSpec('P')
T = TypeVar('T')


# Based off https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/90780#issuecomment-1093943964
class Reawaitable(Generic[T]):
    __sentinel = object()

    def __init__(self, awaitable: Awaitable[T]) -> None:
        self.awaitable = awaitable
        self.result = self.__sentinel

    def __await__(self) -> Iterator[T]:
        if self.result is self.__sentinel:
            self.result = yield from self.awaitable.__await__()
        return self.result


def reawaitable(func: Callable[P, Awaitable[T]]) -> Callable[P, Reawaitable[T]]:
    @wraps(func)
    def wrapper(*args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> Reawaitable[T]:
        return Reawaitable(func(*args, **kwargs))
    return wrapper

    foo: str = 'bar'

@cache

async def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()

## Summary

**Root cause:** `get_typed_signature()` computed `globalns` directly from `getattr(call, "__globals__", {})`. When a route function is decorated with `@functools.wraps()`, `wraps` copies `__annotations__` verbatim (including forward-reference strings) from the wrapped function, but the wrapper's `__globals__` belongs to the *decorator's* module — not the module where the annotations were originally defined. **Fix** (`fastapi/dependencies/utils.py`):

Added a helper that mirrors `typing.get_type_hints()` behavior by dereferencing the `__wrapped__` chain until it reaches the original function, then using *its* `__globals__`:

    unwrapped_call = call
    while hasattr(unwrapped_call, "__wrapped__"):
        unwrapped_call = unwrapped_call.__wrapped__
    return getattr(unwrapped_call, "__globals__", {})
```

This helper is now used by both `get_typed_signature()` (parameter annotations) and `get_typed_return_annotation()` (return annotations), so both paths benefit — the return-annotation path had the same latent bug.

### Problem
In `fastapi/dependencies/utils.py`, `_extract_form_body()` collected extra (undeclared) form parameters via `received_body.items()`. ### Fix
Replaced the `.items()` loop with iteration over `.keys()`, retrieving all values per key via `.getlist()`, matching the approach already used in `_get_multidict_value`:

```python
field_aliases = {field.alias for field in body_fields}

        param_values = received_body.getlist(key)
        if len(param_values) == 1:
            values[key] = param_values[0]
        else:
            values[key] = param_values
```

Per the issue's stated preference, the hybrid behavior was chosen over "always a list": single value → plain string, multiple values → list of strings.

- **Direct behavior probe** of `_extract_form_body` against a real `FormData` confirmed `param2=456&param2=789` → `['456', '789']`, while a lone `other=x` stayed `'x'` (not `['x']`) — both halves of the intended contract.

Exactly one file changed (+6/-2). No test files were modified, and no scratch files were written into `/workspace` — all probing was executed in `/tmp` via the skill harness. Problem Statement:
🐛 Strip whitespaces from `Authorization` header credentials

## Description

Fixes whitespace handling in authorization header parameter extraction to comply with [RFC 6750](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6750#section-2.1).

## Problem

The current implementation preserves leading/trailing whitespace in the extracted credential parameter. While RFC 6750 allows one or more spaces (`1*SP`) between "Bearer" and the token, the token definition (`b64token`) doesn't include whitespace characters, meaning spaces should be treated as separators only.

Problem Statement:
🐛 Fix parsing extra `Form` parameter list

## Description

Currently if we declare Form parameters as model with `extra="allow"` and then pass extra parameter with multiple values, only last value of such parameter will be passed to model validator:

```py
from fastapi import FastAPI, Form
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from pydantic import BaseModel

app = FastAPI()


class Model(BaseModel):
    param: str

    model_config = {"extra": "allow"}

@app.post("/")
async def model_with_extra(data: Model = Form()):
    return data


def test_pass_extra_list():
    client = TestClient(app)
    resp = client.post(
        "/",
        data={
            "param": "123",
            "param2": ["456", "789"],  # Pass a list of values as extra parameter
        },
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert resp.json() == {
        "param": "123",
        "param2": ["456", "789"],
    }
    # AssertionError: assert
    # {'param': '123', 'param2': '789'}
    # ==
    # {'param': '123', 'param2': ['456', '789']}
```

The part of code that adds extra parameters is:

https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/972a967d5d3fa24d450637c36c6b7ad1f1d8c1b6/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py#L901-L903

The problem is in `received_body.items()` - it returns only last value for each key.
To fix this we need to iterate over all keys in `received_body` and get the values using `received_body.getlist(key)`:

```py
    for key in received_body.keys():
        if key not in values:
            param_values = received_body.getlist(key)
            if len(param_values) == 1:
                values[key] = param_values[0]

The `_get_multidict_value` uses `None` to represent both the absence a value in the dict, and a default value of `None` for that field. In the example below this results in an error `AttributeError: 'coroutine' object has no attribute 'foo'`. from functools import cache
from functools import wraps
from typing import Awaitable
from typing import Callable
from typing import Generic
from typing import Iterator
from typing import ParamSpec
from typing import TypeVar

from fastapi import Depends
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseSettings


P = ParamSpec('P')
T = TypeVar('T')


# Based off https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/90780#issuecomment-1093943964
class Reawaitable(Generic[T]):
    __sentinel = object()

    def __init__(self, awaitable: Awaitable[T]) -> None:
        self.awaitable = awaitable
        self.result = self.__sentinel

    def __await__(self) -> Iterator[T]:
        if self.result is self.__sentinel:

        return self.result

    @wraps(func)
    def wrapper(*args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> Reawaitable[T]:

    return wrapper

    return Settings()

messages.content: {"status": "ok", "patch_size": 1619, "files_changed": 1}

Patch submitted successfully.

## Summary

**Root cause:** In `fastapi/_compat/v2.py`, the OpenAPI JSON Schema post-processing treated *any* dictionary key named `"$ref"` as a schema reference. But `"$ref"` is also a legal **JSON Schema attribute name** — a model field can have `alias="$ref"`, which Pydantic emits as a *property key* inside `properties`:

```python
class Model(BaseModel):
    ref: Optional[Sub] = Field(None, alias="$ref")
```

This produced a `properties: {"$ref": {...}}` dict, and both `_replace_refs` and `_remap_definitions_and_field_mappings` then called `.split("/")` on the **dict** value, crashing OpenAPI generation with `AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'split'`.

**Fix (2 surgical edits, one file):**
1. `_replace_refs` — now only treats `key == "$ref"` as a reference when `isinstance(value, str)`; a dict value falls through to normal recursive descent, correctly remapping any nested real references inside it.
2. `_remap_definitions_and_field_mappings` — guards with `schema.get("$ref")` + `isinstance(schema_ref, str)` before splitting, so a model whose field is named `$ref` no longer crashes the name-mapping loop.

**Verification:**
- Unit-level: the previously-crashing schema now round-trips; nested real refs still remapped (`Sub-Input` → `Sub`), and the input schema is not mutated.
- End-to-end: `/openapi.json` returns 200 with `"$ref"` preserved as a property and its inner reference intact; runtime validation/serialization still accept `{"$ref": {"name": "foo"}}`.
- Regression gate: 29/30 neighbor tests pass. The single failure (`test_upload_file`) is a pre-existing async-plugin config issue in a sync file-upload test that never touches OpenAPI generation — unrelated to this change.
- Diff confirmed clean: only `fastapi/_compat/v2.py` (+10/−4), zero test files touched.

## Summary

**Root cause:** In `fastapi/_compat/v2.py`, the OpenAPI JSON Schema post-processing treated *any* dictionary key named `"$ref"` as a schema reference. But `"$ref"` is also a legal **JSON Schema attribute name** — a model field can have `alias="$ref"`, which Pydantic emits as a *property key* inside `properties`:

```python
class Model(BaseModel):
    ref: Optional[Sub] = Field(None, alias="$ref")

This produced a `properties: {"$ref": {...}}` dict, and both `_replace_refs` and `_remap_definitions_and_field_mappings` then called `.split("/")` on the **dict** value, crashing OpenAPI generation with `AttributeError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'split'`.

1. `_replace_refs` — now only treats `key == "$ref"` as a reference when `isinstance(value, str)`; a dict value falls through to normal recursive descent, correctly remapping any nested real references inside it.

    param: str

def test_pass_extra_list():

    resp = client.post(
        "/",
        data={
            "param": "123",
            "param2": ["456", "789"],  # Pass a list of values as extra parameter
        },
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert resp.json() == {
        "param": "123",
        "param2": ["456", "789"],
    }
    # AssertionError: assert
    # {'param': '123', 'param2': '789'}
    # ==
    # {'param': '123', 'param2': ['456', '789']}

https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/972a967d5d3fa24d450637c36c6b7ad1f1d8c1b6/fastapi/dependencies/utils.py#L901-L903

The problem is in `received_body.items()` - it returns only last value for each key.
To fix this we need to iterate over all keys in `received_body` and get the values using `received_body.getlist(key)`:

```py

        if key not in values:
            param_values = received_body.getlist(key)
            if len(param_values) == 1:
                values[key] = param_values[0]
            else:
                values[key] = param_values

This solution parses single value as string

`extra=string` -> `{"extra": "string"}`

but multiple values as list of strings

`extra=string1&extra=string2` -> `{"extra": ["string1", "string2"]}`

We can consider always parse extra parameters as lists

```py

        if key not in values:
            values[key] = received_body.getlist(key)
```

This way for single value we would also have list with one element:

`extra=string` -> `{"extra": ["string"]}`

It's more consistent, but probably not what people expect for single value.

I think we should go with current implementation (single value -> single string, multiple values -> list of strings)

Problem Statement:
🐛 Fix optional sequence handling in `serialize sequence value` with Pydantic V2

Currently the following test code leads to `TypeError: issubclass() arg 1 must be a class` (with Python 3.14 error is different, but the root cause is the same):

```py
from typing import List, Optional

from fastapi import FastAPI, File
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

app = FastAPI()


@app.post("/files")
async def upload_files(files: Optional[List[bytes]] = File(None)):
    if files is None:
        return {"files_count": 0}
    return {"files_count": len(files), "sizes": [len(f) for f in files]}


def test_optional_bytes_list():
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.post(
        "/files",
        files=[("files", b"content1"), ("files", b"content2")],
    )
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.json() == {"files_count": 2, "sizes": [8, 8]}
```

https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/972a967d5d3fa24d450637c36c6b7ad1f1d8c1b6/fastapi/_compat/v2.py#L374

So, we need to unwrap that `Uinion`, take non-None type from its arguments and use it as `origin_type`

Fix #6628 - JSONDecodeError are not deserializable

See issue #6628 for full bug-report

-----

requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError are not deserializable: calling `pickle.dumps` followed by `pickle.loads` will trigger an error.

This is particularly a problem in a process pool, as an attempt to decode json on an invalid json document will result in the entire process pool crashing.

This is due to the MRO of the `requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError` class: the `__reduce__` method called when pickling an instance is not the one from the JSON library parent: two out of three args expected for instantiation will be dropped, and the instance can't be deserialised.

By specifying in the class which parent `__reduce__` method should be called, the bug is fixed as all args are carried over in the resulting pickled bytes.

## Completion Report

### Task
Fix malformed value parsing for `Content-Type` (psf/requests issue #6646) by cleaning up `_parse_content_type_header`.

### Root Cause
In `src/requests/utils.py`, the parameter-parsing loop previously fell back to a sentinel default when a parameter had no `=` sign:

```python
if param:
    key, value = param, True          # <- bogus default
    index_of_equals = param.find("=")
    if index_of_equals != -1:
        key = ...
        value = ...
    params_dict[key.lower()] = value  # <- stored even when malformed
```

A header segment like `no_equals` was stored as `{"no_equals": True}` — a value that could never be used in practice (and would break `.strip("'\"")` consumers such as `get_encoding_from_headers`). Per RFC 1521–9110, an `=` is mandatory for a valid parameter, so malformed entries should simply be ignored.

### Fix Applied
Single surgical edit to `src/requests/utils.py` (lines 517–523) — dropped the unreachable-in-practice `True` default and the now-redundant truthiness guard, assigning only when an `=` is actually present:

```python
for param in params:
    param = param.strip()
    index_of_equals = param.find("=")
    if index_of_equals != -1:
        key = param[:index_of_equals].strip(items_to_strip)
        value = param[index_of_equals + 1 :].strip(items_to_strip)
        params_dict[key.lower()] = value
return content_type, params_dict
```

The `param.strip()` is retained, so empty segments still naturally produce `index_of_equals == -1` and are skipped, preserving the existing `"application/json ; ; "` → `("application/json", {})` behavior.

- `repro-check` isolated assertions passed, covering: `no_equals` now omitted, empty `; ; ` segments ignored, quoted key/value stripping intact, bare `charset` ignored, and normal `charset=utf-8` / multipart filename parsing unchanged.

Problem Statement:
Fix #6628 - JSONDecodeError are not deserializable

See issue #6628 for full bug-report

-----

requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError are not deserializable: calling `pickle.dumps` followed by `pickle.loads` will trigger an error.

This is particularly a problem in a process pool, as an attempt to decode json on an invalid json document will result in the entire process pool crashing.

This is due to the MRO of the `requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError` class: the `__reduce__` method called when pickling an instance is not the one from the JSON library parent: two out of three args expected for instantiation will be dropped, and the instance can't be deserialised.

By specifying in the class which parent `__reduce__` method should be called, the bug is fixed as all args are carried over in the resulting pickled bytes.

Problem Statement:

See issue #6628 for full bug-report

requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError are not deserializable: calling `pickle.dumps` followed by `pickle.loads` will trigger an error.
